newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Energy sees Q2 loss.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Energy sees Q2 loss.

text.p: Wisconsin Energy Corp expects the costs of the cancelled Primergy merger and outage of the Point Beach Nuclear Plant to result in a second quarter loss, chief executive Richard Abdoo said Wednesday.
Abdoo told analysts the company expects a loss in the range of $0.07 to $0.12 per share after a one-time writeoff related to the canceled merger of $0.17 per share.
For the year, he indicated earnings would be well below current expectations.
The First Call consensus estimates are profits of $0.30 per share for the second quarter and $1.94 for the year.
Several extraordinary factors affected second quarter earnings, Abdoo said.

In addition to the one-time merger-related expenses, Wisconsin Energy incurred increased fuel and purchased power costs and non-fuel operations and maintenance costs related to the Point Beach outage.

Most of those factors should not affect results in 1998, Abdoo said, adding he is comfortable with Wall Street's expectations for 1998, assuming the utility receives reasonable rate treatment for 1998.
The consensus estimate for 1998 is $2.09 per share.
The company plans to file later this year with the Wisconsin Public Service Commission to increase rates in 1998.
Abdoo said any future rate requests will not include costs of the canceled merger.
He noted a recent national study has shown Wisconsin Energy's bills to be the lowest among investor-owned utilities serving the 25 largest metropolitan areas of the country.
Abdoo said the company and other Wisconsin utilities are looking at ways to increase the capacities of their transmission lines linking Wisconsin to sources of electric power in other states.
He cited a recent power shortage as an example of the regional challenges facing electric utilities.

"Substantially reducing the likelihood of future shortages will require improvements in the electric power infrastructure, including streamlining the process needed to approve the construction of new electric generating plants. Ensuring reliable service can only happen if we devote additional resources to meet our customers' needs," he said, without providing any specifics.
"The people of Wisconsin don't want to face ongoing power shortages," Abdoo said.
Wisconsin Electric plans to work with other utilities in Wisconsin and surrounding states to develop a regional solution to future power needs and to help guarantee reliability.
Similarly, Wisconsin Energy is nearing the completion of one of the most extensive upgrades, maintenance and equipment replacements at its Point Beach Nuclear Power Plant.
"Point Beach has one of the best records for reliability and production of low-cost electricity among all nuclear plants in the U.S. While the current work has taken some
time to complete, it sets the stage for Point Beach to continue its record of providing cost-effective and reliable electric power well into the next century," Abdoo said.
Abdoo said an additional business strategy will include aggressively pursuing business development activities through Wisconsin Energy's non-utility operations.

"We fully intend to look for acquisition, consolidation and other joint venture opportunities with other energy companies to strengthen our ability to deliver reliable, low-cost power to Wisconsin," Abdoo said.
